extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers of political/social philosophy; readers interested in liberty, individuality, and social improvement
extracted.subtask_description: Expository/philosophical treatment arguing for individuality as a component of human development and social progress, addressing the proper limits of social control, custom, and conformity. Offers normative principles about tolerance, genius, eccentricity, and the relation between liberty and improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individuality as development
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuality is the same thing with development; it is only the cultivation of individuality which produces, or can produce, well-developed human beings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mill argues that the chief standard for human well-being is how close individuals are brought to 'the best thing they can be.' Policies or social arrangements should be judged by whether they allow persons to cultivate and unfold their own faculties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage strong impulses governed by will
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who have most natural feeling, are always those whose cultivated feelings may be made the strongest. If ... his impulses are strong, and are under the government of a strong will, he has an energetic character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong impulses are not an evil if shaped by self-control; society should encourage energetic natures rather than suppress raw energy out of fear of potential evil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit social restraint to preventing harm to others
rubrics_metrics.description: As much compression as is necessary to prevent the stronger specimens of human nature from encroaching on the rights of others, cannot be dispensed with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restraint is justified only insofar as it prevents injury to others; restraints that merely suppress harmless individuality dull and blunt human nature and are unjustified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow different persons to lead different lives
rubrics_metrics.description: To give any fair play to the nature of each, it is essential that different persons should be allowed to lead different lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public opinion and institutions should permit a latitude of ways of living, because different temperaments require different conditions for development; uniform models are inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect originality and genius by freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Genius can only breathe freely in an atmosphere of freedom. Persons of genius ... are more individual than any other people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Society should preserve the 'soil' in which originality grows: tolerate eccentricity and nonconformity because they are the sources of progress and renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of eccentricity and nonconformity as a social good
rubrics_metrics.description: In this age, the mere example of non-conformity, the mere refusal to bend the knee to custom, is itself a service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encouraging eccentricity helps break the tyranny of opinion; the mere demonstration that one may think or act differently is beneficial in a society dominated by mediocrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppose the despotism of custom
rubrics_metrics.description: The despotism of custom is everywhere the standing hindrance to human advancement, being in unceasing antagonism to that disposition to aim at something better than customary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards or institutions that enforce conformity through custom should be criticized because they make societies stationary; plurality of paths fosters improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance should extend to minority and solitary tastes
rubrics_metrics.description: Why then should tolerance, as far as the public sentiment is concerned, extend only to tastes and modes of life which extort acquiescence by the multitude of their adherents?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public tolerance ought to cover even 'what nobody does' — solitary or rare modes of life — rather than only widely practised tastes; minorities deserve protection from social censure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty as the unfailing source of improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The only unfailing and permanent source of improvement is liberty, since by it there are as many possible independent centres of improvement as there are individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating social arrangements or reforms, prefer those that maximize individual liberty because liberty generates multiple independent experiments that drive progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to crushing human faculties in name of obedience
rubrics_metrics.description: To one holding [the Calvinistic] theory of life, crushing out any of the human faculties, capacities, and susceptibilities, is no evil ... man needs no capacity but that of surrendering himself to the will of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject standards that valorize mere obedience at the cost of destroying individual capacities; a sound social norm cultivates faculties rather than annihilates them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware over-control by law and social discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: There has been a time when ... law and discipline ... asserted a power over the whole man, claiming to control all his life in order to control his character ... But society has now fairly got the better of individuality; and the danger ... is not the excess, but the deficiency, of personal impulses and preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical necessity of strict discipline does not justify its present-day overreach; current evaluation should check for excessive legal/social control that eliminates individuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality of paths as criterion of national progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Europe is ... wholly indebted to this plurality of paths for its progressive and many-sided development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess national or cultural health by the diversity of characters, classes, and paths it permits; uniformity indicates stagnation analogous to 'China' in Mill's critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mediocrity as danger when public opinion dominates
rubrics_metrics.description: The general tendency of things throughout the world is to render mediocrity the ascendant power ... public opinion now rules the world ... The only power deserving the name is that of masses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies or cultural norms should be judged negatively when they empower collective mediocrity at the expense of exceptional individual initiative; need counterpoise in the form of pronounced individuality among thinkers/artists/leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different persons require different conditions for development
rubrics_metrics.description: The same things which are helps to one person towards the cultivation of his higher nature, are hindrances to another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public standards or institutional designs should account for individual differences in susceptibilities, tastes, and sources of pleasure; one-size-fits-all solutions inhibit many people's flourishing.
